_provenance: A body that stands under its own weight. The genome is a skeleton; the measure reports structural facts about the grown body. It never mentions legs — legs, if they appear, are the ANSWER. Design Law 1: the simplest rules produce the richest order. Three degenerate optima (lollipop, blob-on-stilts, mast-with-outriggers) proved that static geometry can be gamed; the walker domain picks up where this ends.

walls.stands: The centre of gravity MUST project inside the support polygon. stands=0 means it is a thing lying down — not a creature. This is THE gate: every other measure is meaningless if the body cannot hold itself up.
walls.tip_deg: The body MUST survive a real tilt before toppling. Below 22 degrees means a small slope sends it over — the lollipop (boulder on a pole) tipped at 7.8 degrees. A quadruped starts at ~26.6. This is the term that makes carrying mass high COST you the robustness needed to keep it there.
walls.height: The body MUST be carried clear of the ground. Below 0.22 body lengths means the body is a pancake — perfectly stable, maximally useless. A pancake wins every structural check and cannot walk.
walls.volume: Volume MUST stay bounded. Above 0.01 means a single enormous bone dominates — the lollipop exploit: mass goes as r^2, so one bone free-rides. Charging per bone count lets one enormous bone escape; charging volume catches it.
walls.symmetry: The body SHOULD exhibit bilateral symmetry. Real development is symmetric because it is cheap, not because symmetry is fitness — but below 0.65 means the body is a random spray of limbs, and natural selection does not produce that.
